def-one-step-ode-method-local-defect-ord:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be open, and consider a first-order IVP and solution in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. A **one-step method** is a family of maps $\Psi_h(t,v)$, defined for admitted times $t$, positive step sizes $h$, and states $v$, whose value is the method's approximation at time $t+h$ from the single input state $v$ at time $t$. It does not use earlier numerical states.

If $y$ is an exact solution on an interval containing $[t,t+h]$, the **local defect** is

$$\delta_h(t;y):=\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h).$$

Let $K\subseteq D$ be a fixed compact time-state set. The method has **uniform local order $p$ on $K$ along $y$** if there are constants $C\ge0$ and $h_0>0$, independent of the admitted starting time $t$ and step $0<h\le h_0$, such that

$$\|\delta_h(t;y)\|_2\le C h^{p+1}$$

whenever the exact solution graph on $[t,t+h]$ and the associated method time-state inputs, stages, and outputs under consideration lie in $K$. Here $p$ is a positive integer and $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

The method has **one-step Lipschitz stability on $K$** with constant $L\ge0$ if

$$\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2$$

for every admitted step size $h$, admitted time $t$, and input states $u,v$ with $(t,u),(t,v)\in K$. This is a bound on the change in one step; it is separate from absolute or linear stability regions and does not itself assert a global error estimate.
lem-time-along-ode-solution-derivative-b:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, let $V\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $f:V\to\mathbb R^d$ have continuous first partial derivatives, and let $y:I\to\mathbb R^d$ solve $y'=f(t,y)$ on an open interval $I$. Fix $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subset I$ such that $(s,y(s))\in V$ for every $s\in[a,b]$. Suppose finite constants $F_j,M_{t,i},M_{ij}\ge0$ satisfy for all $s\in[a,b]$

$$|f_j(s,y(s))|\le F_j,\qquad |\partial_t f_i(s,y(s))|\le M_{t,i},\qquad |\partial_{z_j}f_i(s,y(s))|\le M_{ij}\qquad(1\le i,j\le d).$$

Define $g_i(s):=f_i(s,y(s))$ and $B_i:=M_{t,i}+\sum_{j=1}^dM_{ij}F_j$. Then $g_i$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$, and

$$g_i'(s)=\partial_t f_i(s,y(s))+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{z_j}f_i(s,y(s))f_j(s,y(s)),\qquad |g_i'(s)|\le B_i.$$
thm-forward-euler-one-step-consistency-a:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, and let $V\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be an open time-state domain whose fibers $V_t:=\{z:(t,z)\in V\}$ are open and convex. Let $K\subset V$ be compact. Let $f:V\to\mathbb R^d$ have continuous first partial derivatives, and suppose $y$ is a solution of $y'=f(t,y)$, $y(0)=y_0$, on an open interval containing $[0,T]$, with graph on $[0,T]$ contained in $K$. For each local defect under consideration, require the Euler input and output time-state pairs to lie in $K$; the exact solution segment already lies in $K$.

For $1\le i,j\le d$, assume finite constants $F_j,M_{t,i},M_{ij},L\ge0$ satisfy throughout $V$

$$|f_j(t,z)|\le F_j,\qquad |\partial_t f_i(t,z)|\le M_{t,i},\qquad |\partial_{z_j}f_i(t,z)|\le M_{ij},\qquad \|D_yf(t,z)w\|_2\le L\|w\|_2\quad(w\in\mathbb R^d).$$

Here $D_yf$ is the matrix with entries $\partial_{z_j}f_i$, and the last inequality defines the operator bound used below. The forward Euler map is $\Psi_h(t,v)=v+h f(t,v)$. Then, with $B_i:=M_{t,i}+\sum_{j=1}^dM_{ij}F_j$, for every $t\in[0,T)$ and $h>0$ with $t+h\le T$ whose Euler input and output pairs lie in $K$, its local defect satisfies

$$\|\delta_h(t;y)\|_2\le \frac{h^2}{2}\left(\sum_{i=1}^d B_i^2\right)^{1/2},$$

so it has uniform local order one on $K$ along $y|_{[0,T]}$, with $h_0=T$. For every $t\in[0,T]$, every admitted $h>0$, and every $u,v\in V_t$,

$$\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2.$$

This is a local defect and one-step stability result. It does not assert a global error estimate or an order for any other named method.
